arg_convention: (record, length, align, flag, shift) = (rdi, rsi, rdx, ecx low byte, r8d); returns node pointer or NULL; single ret 0x63b132b
corrections_to_earlier_packets: #225 confirmed: the four slot-head call sites (0x63b0bc7, 0x63b1131, 0x63b1490, 0x63b14ed) are exactly this function's calls, and FDE 0x63b0980..0x63b15e9 is one function with one ret and 8 calls.
#225 refined: replace sites 0x63b1490 and 0x63b14ed are the same best-replacement step in the compiler's duplicated loop heads, not two different operations.

#224 confirmed: record layout (bitmap, 32-byte slots, cached key at [T+0x10]/[T+0x18]) matches exactly, and the .bss table at 0x6728180 is the same table #224 cited; the size helper here (0x63e8c80) is a distinct sibling of #224's 0x63e8bf0.

#216/#218 refined: the allocator pool's slot array uses a 16-byte stride and is a different table from the record's 32-byte class slots; the slot-entry prefix and the chain helpers operating on it are shared.

phases.phase1_exact: flag nonzero: slot T = P + (index+1)*32; empty test 0x63abcf0(T); else slot-head 0x63abd00(T) returns head
phases.phase1_scan: flag zero: bitmap scan for first set class >= index; iterate set classes, table[c]>>shift <= A+L-0x1000 required, keep smallest stored cached key, slot-head on each new best
phases.phase2: rdx > 0x1000 and phase 1 found nothing: scan set classes in [idx(L), idx(A+L-0x1000)); slot-head each; return first head whose range covers (aligned base within [base, base+size), remainder >= L)

record_layout.bitmap: P+0x00..P+0x20, one bit per class, 4 words cover 200 classes
record_layout.slot: T = P + (i+1)*32, 32 bytes per class; [T] head, [T+8] second word

return_contract: node pointer or NULL; NULL iff no eligible class (phase 1) and no covering head (phase 2); single ret 0x63b132b with rax = rsi
slot_relation: record 32-byte class slots (this function, #224) vs allocator pool 16-byte slots (#216: pool+0xa8..0xf28, stride 16); shared [slot]/[slot+8] prefix; only record entries carry the cached-key words
threshold: r13 = A + L - 0x1000 with A = (rdx + 0xfff) & ~0xfff; classes >= idx(r13) are certainly big enough (max alignment slack for page-aligned bases is A - 0x1000)
